after_landing.notes: Archives the plan folder only when its gaps list has no open entry; with an open gap, skip this step and leave the folder live.

release_levels.reason: Twenty new Mac tools and six new Mac packs are new behavior; no repo consumer changes anything.

units.title: Mac packs and the sample values file for the extras

shared_files.why: every human-facing doc; the earlier units report DOCS FALSIFIED lines and never edit a doc

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 lands runnable bash code (the task scripts of claude-cli, pstree, telegram and tailscale, and two fish files). One review unit in wave 2 covers U1 and U2.
decisions.rejected: No review unit: the wave review alone does not run /security-review.

decisions.decision: Can the 16 plans of the merge run in parallel?
decisions.ruling: No. The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires, because most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there. This plan requires 2026-11-04-macos-tools-base-shells.

decisions.decision: Do the undeclared edges of the old tools become depends?
decisions.ruling: Yes. 1password gets git in depends, because it contributes to git. claude-cli gets depends = ["cli"], because its settings.json.tmpl reads .all.cli.

decisions.decision: How much of each old file changes in the port?
decisions.ruling: Each shipped file is a byte copy of the old file. Only the header lines change, and the text of each required message changes to name [tools.<name>] of macos.toml. A task body keeps its commands as they are, also where the repo task rules ask for mise x --. Each trailing comment of an old mise fragment line stays as a TOML comment on the same entry in tools.toml.
decisions.rejected: Rewrite the Mac task bodies to the repo task rules; this changes the live behavior and breaks the byte compare of the scratch-HOME comparison.

decisions.decision: In which order does a pack of macos/packs.toml list its members?
decisions.ruling: In the order of the old tools list of that pack in MS/tools/packs.toml. A plan that adds a member inserts it at its old position, so after P14 each pack has the old order.

decisions.decision: Does the plan add test cases?
decisions.ruling: No new test case. test:macos-tools renders every tool that macos/examples/macos.toml selects and parses every JSON, YAML and TOML output, so U2's selection of the 20 tools is their test.
decisions.rejected: One test case for each new tool.

decisions.decision: How does the sample values file select the 20 tools?
decisions.ruling: One [tools.<name>] table for each of the 20 tools, empty except [tools.1password] with ssh_vault = "Sample". This follows MS/tests/setup-sync/sample-config/macos-setup.toml, which selects every tool outside pack base.
decisions.rejected: [packs.<name>] tables; they select only the default = true members, so test:macos-tools does not render the other members.

decisions.decision: Does codeburn keep node in depends?
decisions.ruling: codeburn gets depends = ["claude-cli"] only. The mise depends of npm:codeburn names node and pnpm, so the engine adds the node tool; a second node in depends repeats it, which the CLAUDE.md rule forbids.
decisions.rejected: Keep node in depends as the old tools.toml has it.

decisions.decision: Does tools.toml keep the old header line of a fragment?
decisions.ruling: The old `# Generated by macos-setup: ...` line of each fragment goes: tools.toml is not shipped, so it carries no header. Every other comment stays.
decisions.rejected: Keep the old header line as a comment.

decisions.decision: Does a security finding in content that this plan imports unchanged from macos-setup stop the run?
decisions.ruling: User ruling 2026-11-05, given at D14 of 2026-11-04-macos-tools-base-core for plans 11 to 14: no. A security finding in content that is byte for byte from macos-setup, apart from the changes that this plan names, is accepted for this import. It does not stop the run, and the content does not change. The run records each such finding as an open gap with its severity and location, for one security plan after the run. A finding in code that this plan writes or changes stops the run as before.
decisions.rejected: Stop on each finding in imported content.
